summary:
AstraSense – Deep Space Psychological & Physiological Survival System is an AI-assisted astronaut health monitoring platform designed to improve crew safety and well-being during long-duration space missions.

We developed an Android application featuring a Dual-Layer Dashboard that integrates physiological health monitoring, psychological assessment, radiation exposure tracking, sleep and fatigue analysis, cognitive performance testing, and mission intelligence.

AstraSense utilizes NASA open-data resources and space-weather information to support health-risk identification, provide data-driven insights, and assist astronauts and mission controllers in making informed decisions. It also incorporates emergency-response workflows and crew wellness recommendations.

The project addresses critical challenges of deep-space exploration, including radiation exposure, microgravity-related health risks, psychological stress, isolation, sleep disruption, and delayed medical assistance.

Why is it important? As humanity prepares for extended lunar and Mars missions, continuous astronaut health monitoring is essential. AstraSense aims to make space exploration safer and more sustainable by combining AI-assisted health analysis, scientific data, and integrated mission-support technologies to protect the people behind every space mission.
details:
AstraSense is an AI-assisted astronaut health-monitoring and mission-risk assessment platform designed to address the psychological, physiological, and environmental challenges astronauts face during long-duration space missions. As humanity moves toward extended lunar exploration, Mars missions, and deep-space travel, maintaining astronauts' physical and mental health becomes increasingly important. AstraSense aims to provide an intelligent digital support system that helps monitor astronaut wellbeing, identify potential health risks, and support timely mission-safety decisions.

1. What Exactly Does AstraSense Do?

AstraSense combines astronaut health assessment, mission-risk analysis, NASA open-space data integration, and AI-powered assistance into a unified platform.

Its major capabilities include:

  • Health Assessment: Evaluates astronaut health-related information and identifies potential physiological concerns.
  • Mission Risk Assessment: Uses a dedicated Mission Risk Score Service to assess and communicate potential mission-related risks.
  • NASA Space Weather Monitoring: Retrieves relevant space-weather information, including Solar Energetic Particle (SEP) events, Solar Flares (FLR), and Coronal Mass Ejections (CME), through NASA's DONKI API.
  • NASA Open Data Exploration: Searches NASA's open scientific datasets to provide relevant space research information.
  • AI Space Assistant: Integrates Google's Gemini through Firebase AI Logic to provide AI-assisted information and astronaut support.
  • Psychomotor Vigilance Testing (PVT): Includes a reaction-time testing interface to help assess alertness and cognitive performance.
  • Offline Data Accessibility: Maintains locally stored information and embedded mission datasets to support functionality when communication with Earth is unavailable.

2. How Does It Work?

AstraSense follows a multi-layered software architecture.

Layer 1 – Data Collection and Integration

The application retrieves relevant NASA datasets and space-weather information through external APIs. It also supports health-assessment workflows and mission-related information processing.

Layer 2 – Health and Mission Risk Analysis

The HealthAssessmentService evaluates health-related information, while the MissionRiskScoreService processes risk-related parameters to generate understandable assessment results. These services help transform information into meaningful health and mission-safety indicators.

Layer 3 – AI-Powered Assistance

SpaceAiAssistant integrates Google's Gemini AI through Firebase AI Logic. It provides an intelligent conversational interface for accessing space-related information and obtaining AI-assisted explanations.

Layer 4 – Visualization and User Interface

The application presents information through interactive dashboards, custom biometric visualizations, spacecraft-inspired interfaces, health indicators, and mission-risk gauges. This allows users to understand complex information more easily.

Layer 5 – Offline and Data Synchronization Support

Room/SQLite provides local data storage, while an offline queue helps preserve information during connectivity interruptions. NASA EVA, DONKI, and Human Research Program (HRP) records are also embedded to provide fallback information during communication blackouts.

3. What Benefits Does It Have?

  • Helps organize astronaut health and mission-risk information in one platform.
  • Supports early identification and assessment of potential health-related concerns.
  • Provides access to NASA space-weather information relevant to radiation-related mission risks.
  • Offers AI-assisted explanations and information access.
  • Includes reaction-time testing to support cognitive alertness assessment.
  • Improves access to stored mission information during communication interruptions.
  • Provides a foundation for more intelligent astronaut health-support systems for long-duration missions.

4. What Do We Hope to Achieve?

Our primary goal is to contribute to safer and more sustainable human space exploration.

We envision AstraSense evolving into a comprehensive astronaut survival-support platform that combines physiological monitoring, psychological wellbeing assessment, environmental risk analysis, and AI-assisted decision support.

In the future, we aim to expand its capabilities through real wearable-device integration, continuous biometric monitoring, advanced behavioral analysis, predictive health-risk models, and improved mission simulations.

Ultimately, we want AstraSense to help address one of the greatest challenges of deep-space exploration: keeping astronauts healthy, mentally resilient, and safe when they are millions of kilometers away from Earth.

5. Tools, Technologies, Programming Languages, and Software Used

Programming Languages

  • Kotlin 2.2.10
  • Java
  • TypeScript
  • JavaScript
  • Python
  • SQL

Android Development

  • Android Studio
  • Jetpack Compose
  • Material Design 3

Backend and Database

  • Node.js
  • Python
  • SQLAlchemy
  • PostgreSQL / Cloud SQL
  • Firebase Authentication
  • Cloud Firestore
  • Firebase App Check
  • Room Database / SQLite

AI Integration

  • Google Gemini AI
  • Firebase AI Logic

API and Networking

  • NASA Open Data Portal (CKAN API)
  • NASA DONKI API
  • Retrofit
  • OkHttp
  • Moshi

Data Sources

  • NASA Open Data datasets
  • NASA Space Weather Database (DONKI)
  • Solar Energetic Particle (SEP) records
  • Solar Flare (FLR) records
  • Coronal Mass Ejection (CME) records
  • NASA Human Research Program (HRP) information
  • NASA EVA-related records

Development and Design

  • Android Studio
  • Custom Jetpack Compose UI components
  • Material 3 design system
  • Custom spacecraft, human-wireframe, biometric-radar, and mission-risk visualizations

Conclusion

AstraSense is more than an ordinary health-monitoring application. It is a foundation for an intelligent astronaut health and mission-safety ecosystem. By combining AI assistance, health assessment, NASA's open scientific resources, space-weather monitoring, cognitive testing, and offline data support, the project explores how technology can help protect human life during future deep-space missions.

Our vision is simple: Explore farther, understand better, and keep humanity safer beyond Earth.
